what_it_does: Testing a chip after it comes off the manufacturing line (called post-silicon test engineering) is a highly specialized job that normally requires experts who know the chip's quirks inside out. This paper explores using large language models (AI systems trained on vast amounts of text, like the ones that power chatbots) to automate some of that expert work. The proposed system works in two stages: first the AI interprets what the engineer is asking, then it translates that into real actions on the existing test equipment. A case study called the Intelligent Engineering Assistant shows the system successfully carrying out test tasks on its own, though the abstract is light on specifics about what kinds of tests it handles or how reliably it performs.
